requirements.requirement: Successful changes to /etc/inventory.conf on node1 are recorded in the system audit log with key inventory-config.
requirements.summary: A post-restart write changed the file hash and was then restored. The corresponding /var/log/audit/audit.log event identifies /etc/inventory.conf, success=yes, and key=inventory-config.

requirements.requirement: Unsuccessful changes to /etc/inventory.conf on node1 are recorded in the system audit log with key inventory-config.
requirements.summary: A post-restart unprivileged write failed with permission denied without changing the file, and the audit log records the attempt against /etc/inventory.conf with success=no, EACCES, and key=inventory-config.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct post-restart tests demonstrate successful and denied changes being written to the system audit log with the required path and key. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and auditd, the rule, target data, and functional logging recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently confirm the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Enabling and starting auditd (cmd-3c16c4afb4f5435e), installing the audit rule (cmd-1fb427fde2444dc1), and loading it (cmd-be9d4036bd074f50) directly established the requested auditing. Both successful probe mutations were bounded and fully reverted, including removal of their temporary files (cmd-bd2822690b974ba2, cmd-e0521d07e4c14917); denied probes did not alter the target. The reboot mutation (cmd-4c3c883d49ba4504) served the mandatory restart protocol. Final evidence shows the original target hash, ownership, and mode, no failed services, unchanged logical socket exposure, and healthy package state.
